data.scenario_text: A wheelchair ramp is to be built beside the steps to a building. The ramp is <m>42</m> feet long and rises <m>3</m> feet to reach the door.
data.find_task: Find the angle the ramp makes with the ground. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked and only the two given lengths written in: the leg opposite \theta is 3\text{ ft} and the hypotenuse is 42\text{ ft}. The third side is not given, so it stays unlabeled, and the angle should not be filled in.

Part (b). Both given quantities are lengths and the unknown is an angle, so the answer comes from an inverse function. In the triangle the given sides are the leg opposite \theta and the hypotenuse; the ratio built from exactly those two sides is sine, \sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, so we solve \sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} for \theta using the inverse sine.

Substituting and computing, \theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{42}\right).

This gives \theta \approx 4.10^\circ, so the angle the ramp makes with the ground is \boxed{4.10^\circ}.
